questions.prompt: Plan an experiment to test this prediction: ‘The more hot water you add to 100 g of cold water, the higher the final temperature.’
questions.modelAnswer: Start with 100 g of water at 20 °C in an insulated cup each time. Independent variable: the mass of 80 °C water added (50, 100, 150, 200 g). Dependent variable: the final temperature, measured with a laboratory thermometer after stirring. Control variables: the starting temperatures, the same cup, the same stirring time, reading the thermometer the same way. Repeat each mix three times. Plot final temperature against mass of hot water added.
rubric: Independent variable: mass of hot water added
Dependent variable: final temperature with a thermometer
Repeats and a graph or table
questions.explain: Criterion B: turn a prediction into a fair, measurable test.

questions.text: When two objects reach the same temperature, heat stops flowing. They are in thermal ___.
